At a glance

Where the pairs come from

TreebanksUniversal Dependencies sentences, with the written text and any multiword tokens.
Agreement instancesEvery head–dependent pair of a condition (verb and subject, noun and adjective, …) with its morphological features.
Decision treesPer language and condition a tree learns when the two tokens agree; only agreeing configurations are kept, with their leaf recorded.
Minimal pairsThe dependent is reinflected for another feature value, and the written forms of both sentences are built.
This benchmarkA balanced sample of those pairs, up to per language.

Using the data

The benchmark is a directory with two parquet files per language, joined by pair_id, next to a manifest.json (settings, treebank counts before and after, languages left out) and a stats.json (the counts and distributions on this page).


  
ColumnMeaning

    
phenomenon, deprelThe condition of the pair (such as svNa) and its relation (nsubj; empty for noun-phrase conditions).

    
pair_idStable id of the pair (language, condition, relation and the swapped token), the same across rebuilds with the same source.

    
sen / wrong_senThe original sentence and the sentence with the swapped word (the pair a model is scored on), as written (contractions such as du or ins restored).

    
sen_hashHash of the original sentence, to spot edits to the treebank.

    
feature_valsOriginal and swapped value, such as Sing -> Plur; | lists values the swapped form also spells.

    
swap_kind, swap_idx, swap_<kind>Which token was reinflected, its position in the sentence, and the new form.

    
leaf_id, second_chanceThe decision-tree leaf the pair stems from, and whether its fit was accepted at the laxer second-chance accuracy.

    
surface_statusHow the written form was built (plain, contracted, merged, uncontracted, …). uncontracted_unattested marks a guessed form (components joined by spaces, never seen in the treebanks); such pairs are drawn only when a language has nothing else.

    
alt_phenomenaOther phenomena in which the same sentence pair was found; the pair is kept only under the rarest of them.

    
treebank, sent_idWhere the sentence comes from.

  

  
<Language>.parquet holds these columns plus the attractor flags, the lemmas, POS tags, order and distance of both tokens (idx_a/idx_b, word_order, distance). features/<Language>.parquet holds the same pairs with every tree and feature column of the source tables.

  
import pandas as pd
pairs = pd.read_parquet("output/benchmark/German.parquet")
pairs[["sen", "wrong_sen", "feature_vals", "phenomenon"]].head()
